claim.claim-text: 1. An unmanned air-vehicle with deployable components, UAVDC, comprising:

a fuselage; a wing (110) arrangement segmented in a left wing (110) section and a right wing (110) section to enable variable sweep at approximately a lateral plane of symmetry between the left wing (110) section and the right wing (110) section, the wing (110) arrangement being configurable in a first arrangement, a second arrangement, and third arrangement, wherein the first arrangement comprises the left wing (110) section and the right wing (110) section stowed against the fuselage at a first sweep deployment angle, wherein the second arrangement comprises the wing (110) arrangement fully deployed for flight at a second sweep deployment angle, and wherein the third arrangement comprises the wing (110) arrangement deployed in any sweep deployment angle between the first sweep deployment angle and the second sweep deployment angle; and a sweeping means configured to pivot the left wing (110) section and the right wing (110) section to enable the wing (110) arrangement to sweep from the first arrangement to the second arrangement at any sweep deployment angle, said sweeping means being covered by a flexible fairing (130) positioned relatively at a base of the left wing (110) section and the right wing (110) section.
2. The UAVDC of claim 1, wherein the wing (110) arrangement is further configured to telescope to increase the wingspan of the second arrangement.

3. The UAVDC of claim 1, wherein the left wing (110) section and the right wing (110) section are stacked against the fuselage, in the first arrangement, with the left wing (110) section vertically offset from the right wing (110) section.

said fairing (130) comprises at least one slit and at least one cutout, the fairing (130) being configured to: open by flexing to allow the left wing (110) section and the right wing (110) section to be stowed under the fairing (130) in the first arrangement, and close to provide aerodynamic advantage in the second arrangement.

5. The UAVDC of claim 4, wherein the at least one cutout of the fairing (130) is configured to accommodate a profile of the base of the left wing (110) section and the right wing (110) section in the second wing (110) arrangement.

6. The UAVDC of claim 4, wherein the fairing (130) creates a first amount of tension in an open configuration corresponding to the first arrangement of the left wing (110) section and the right wing (110) section, wherein the first amount of tension causes the fairing (130) to close when the left wing (110) section and the right wing (110) section reach the second arrangement.
7. The UAVDC of claim 6, wherein the fairing (130) in the open arrangement buckles at a location of the at least one slit to accommodate the first arrangement.
8. The UAVDC of claim 7, wherein fairing (130) does not buckle at the location of the at least one slit to accommodate the second arrangement.

9. The UAVDC of claim 4, further comprising magnets configured to secure the fairing (130) in to the fuselage in a closed configuration corresponding to the second arrangement of the left wing (110) section and the right wing (110) section.
10. The UAVDC of claim 4, wherein the fairing (130) is configured in an orientation to facilitate buckling and flexibility in a composite laminate by using +/-45 degree composite plies.

11. The UAVDC of claim 1, further comprising: at least one stabilizer (125) configured to deploy from a first stabilizer (125) configuration stowed against the fuselage at a first deployment angle to a second stabilizer (125) configuration deployed for flight at a second deployment angle, wherein the at least one stabilizer (125) can be deflected/rotated about its spanwise axis to provide positive flight control while in the second stabilizer (125) configuration.

12. The UAVDC of claim 11, further comprising at least one spring, wherein the at least one spring is configured to force the at least one stabilizer (125) from the first stabilizer (125) configuration to the second stabilizer (125) configuration.
13. The UAVDC of claim 11, further comprising:

a servo configured to move a control horn coupled to the at least one stabilizer (125) for rotating the at least one stabilizer (125) about its spanwise axis, and wherein the control horn is configured to remain in a relatively fixed position as the at least one stabilizer (125) deploys from the first stabilizer (125) configuration to the second stabilizer (125) configuration.

14. The UAVDC of claim 1, further comprising a propeller (135), wherein the propeller (135) comprises at least one blade configured to fold into a first propeller (135) arrangement and expand in a second propeller (135) arrangement.
15. The UAVDC of claim 14, wherein the fuselage comprises at least one groove configured to receive at least one blade of the propeller (135) in the first propeller (135) arrangement.
